Package com.wgblackmon.aihealthcare.infrastructure.config

Class AppConfig

java.lang.Object
com.wgblackmon.aihealthcare.infrastructure.config.AppConfig
@Configuration @EnableCaching @EnableScheduling public class AppConfig extends Object
Spring configuration class that wires the application-layer service as a bean.

Why is NewsletterService not annotated with @Service? NewsletterService lives in the application layer, which is intentionally free of Spring annotations. This keeps the application layer testable without a Spring context — unit tests construct it directly with mock ports and a real NewsletterRenderer, no framework involved.

This @Configuration class acts as the wiring bridge: it lives in infrastructure/config (where Spring is allowed), pulls in the outbound-port adapters that Spring has auto-detected via @Component, constructs a stateless NewsletterRenderer, and manually builds the NewsletterService.

@EnableScheduling activates @Scheduled methods in FeedHarvestScheduler. @EnableConfigurationProperties registers FeedSourceProperties for @ConfigurationProperties binding.

The PgVectorStore bean is auto-configured by the spring-ai-starter-vector-store-pgvector starter — no manual bean registration is needed here.

    • demoExpirationFilter

      @Bean public org.springframework.boot.web.servlet.FilterRegistrationBean<DemoExpirationFilter> demoExpirationFilter(AppUserPort appUserPort, SubscriberPort subscriberPort)
      Registers the DemoExpirationFilter as a servlet filter that runs after the Spring Security filter chain.

      This filter checks DEMO users on each request and transitions expired demos to FREE_PENDING. Registered via FilterRegistrationBean rather than in SecurityConfig to avoid adding port dependencies to the security configuration (which would impact all 35+ WebMvcTest classes).

      Parameters:
      appUserPort - Adapter implementing app user persistence (auto-detected).
      subscriberPort - Adapter implementing subscriber persistence (auto-detected).
      Returns:
      The filter registration bean.

    • trendOrchestrationService

      @Bean public TrendOrchestrationService trendOrchestrationService(ArticleIngestionPort articleIngestionPort, TrendTopicExtractionPort trendTopicExtractionPort, TrendSnapshotPort trendSnapshotPort, ArticleScoringPort articleScoringPort, TrendSummaryPort trendSummaryPort, @Value("${aihealthcare.tech-trends.scoring-enabled:false}") boolean scoringEnabled, @Value("${aihealthcare.tech-trends.score-threshold:7}") int scoreThreshold, @Value("${aihealthcare.deep-research.max-summaries-per-run:5}") int maxSummariesPerRun, @Value("${aihealthcare.trends.rising-limit:20}") int maxTopics)
      Creates the TrendOrchestrationService bean that implements DetectTrendsUseCase.

      Uses LLM-based topic extraction instead of n-gram frequency counting. The TrendTopicExtractionPort adapter (auto-detected) sends article titles to an LLM to identify emerging themes.

      Parameters:
      articleIngestionPort - Adapter implementing article fetching (auto-detected).
      trendTopicExtractionPort - LLM-based topic extraction adapter (auto-detected).
      trendSnapshotPort - Adapter implementing snapshot persistence (auto-detected).
      articleScoringPort - Adapter implementing article scoring (auto-detected).
      trendSummaryPort - Adapter implementing deep research summaries (auto-detected).
      scoringEnabled - whether to enable LLM article scoring.
      scoreThreshold - minimum score to include articles.
      maxSummariesPerRun - maximum deep research summaries per run.
      maxTopics - maximum trend topics to extract per window.
      Returns:
      The wired TrendOrchestrationService instance.
